correctness.rationale: The weak-barrier projection inequality is applied to every normalized cube diagonal. Averaging yields an integrated first-absolute-moment deficit at most \(2\delta\). The exact Rademacher fourth-moment identity gives \(1-\Phi(v)\ge(1-\sum_i v_i^4)/(\sqrt n+1)^2\). On \(J_\beta\), the capped-simplex maximization gives \(1-\sum_i v_i^4\ge2\sin^2\beta\cos^2\beta\). Integrating proves exactly the stated constant. Boundary cases and normalizations were checked against the source definitions; no finite experiment is used as the universal proof.

Replacing the higher-dimensional cube estimate from a sublinear deficit power by a linear law is a structurally stronger near-equality statement, with an explicit coefficient and direct applicability to the weak-barrier framework used for future Jones-bound improvements.
